block-guide:
CONTACT-FORM-7/CONTACT-FORM-SELECTOR (Contact Form 7) Shows an existing Contact Form 7 form. The block exists only while Contact Form 7 is active. It does not create forms: find the form with list-forms, or make it with create-cf7-form first. THE SHORTCODE INSIDE IS WHAT RUNS The block has no render callback: the page shows the [contact-form-7 …] shortcode written inside its
. The attributes in the comment only feed the editor, which rebuilds the shortcode from them and reports the block as invalid when the text differs. Write both from the same values. MARKUP (as the editor saves it)
[contact-form-7 id="" title="
"]
- id: the form's post id (list-forms / get-cf7-form). title: the form's title, as is. - A form chosen in the editor also gets "hash" in the comment, and the shortcode then carries the hash instead of the number: {"id":597,"hash":"0d72c63","title":"…"} -> [contact-form-7 id="0d72c63" title="…"]. Keep such a block as it is; write new ones with the id. - Optional attributes, appended to the shortcode in this order when set: htmlId -> html_id="…", htmlName -> html_name="…", htmlTitle -> html_title="…", htmlClass -> html_class="…", "output":"raw_form" -> output="raw_form". Example: {"id":,"title":"","htmlClass":""} -> [contact-form-7 id="" title="" html_class=""] PITFALLS - Changing only "id" in the comment changes nothing on the page; change the shortcode with it. - Contact Form 7 looks the form up by the shortcode's id, then by its title; when neither matches, the page shows "Error: Contact form not found." - A page that shows the form does not prove that its mail is delivered. CHECK Open the page: a with the form's fields. Reopen the editor: the block shows no invalid-content warning.
